per_shot.note: Faceted white wyrm with a strong hex eye and open jaw reads as a creature, but it sits pale-on-pale inside a uniformly blown-out cyan pool rectangle that outshines everything and flattens the dark.
Teeth, eye and segmented body read well close-up; the pool is a flat bright slab with a hard glowing top line, and the wyrm has no glow of its own separate from the water.
Pretty ice-star in a teal tile, but it looks nothing like the cyan crack-vein veinlight ore, so it is not disguised; the glow stays inside a hard square and barely touches neighbouring rock.
Nice faceted star and faint sparkle, but the tile is a flat gradient square with a hard edge, and nothing hints at the bite (subtle tell absent or too loud depending on read).
Best of the set: spiky sea-green domes read as a hazard at play size, and their light washes the glass tiles and rock below in true MAELIS green against real darkness.
Silhouettes, spines and the light pool on the stone hold up; the overlap between the middle two domes clips to pure white and merges them into one blob.

Glowing faceted eye in a sea-green swirl reads as a current with an eye and lights the floor below; the swirl is soft smears plus scattered dark dashes that drift toward noise, and the threat reach is vague.
Eye reads like a flat UI ring rather than a body part; the pod's lamp beam and the swirl merge into a white-green blowout at the bottom centre.

top_issues.issue: Brinewyrm pool is an over-bright flat slab
top_issues.why: The whole pool is one near-uniform luminous cyan rectangle with a hard bright surface line. It flattens the dark, becomes the brightest thing in frame, and swallows the pale wyrm, so the creature does not read as lit by itself. 05-cryos has a glowing pool, but its value falls off with depth and toward the edges.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Drop the pool's base emission and add a depth gradient (brighter near the surface or a glow core, darker toward the bottom and edges). Let the wyrm carry its own cyan-white bioglow, a light at the head/eye that pools on the rim stones, so it is the value peak and not the water.

top_issues.issue: Frostbloom is not disguised as veinlight ore
top_issues.why: CRYOS veinlight ore reads as a tile with glowing cyan branching cracks. Frostbloom is a white spiky star burst that looks like a different object, so the trap is either obvious or unrelated. The brief asks for a beautiful ore with a subtle tell.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build it from the veinlight vocabulary (same cyan crack-vein tile and bloom), then add one tell: e.g. veins that radiate from a single centre point, a faint slow pulse, or a frost rime and a few needle tips at the tile edge. Keep the full star burst for the reveal/bite.

top_issues.why: The light is confined to a hard-edged square with a gradient inside it, and adjacent tiles are not visibly washed by it apart from the headlamp. That breaks the 'glow that lands' rule.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft bloom and a small point light so the faces of neighbouring tiles pick up cyan, as the veinlight tiles in the stillwalkers frame do.

top_issues.issue: Riptide's swirl drifts toward noise and the eye looks like a UI ring
top_issues.why: Soft gradient smears plus many small dashes, some reading dark/black, give a busy particle field rather than a chunky low-poly current. The eye is a flat bright ring with a diamond pupil, which reads more like a portal icon than part of a creature. The extent of the danger (where the pull starts) is hard to judge.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Fewer, broader, faceted ribbon bands with a clear spiral and a defined outer edge marking its reach, all particles in light sea-green (no dark specks). Give the eye depth (lid or rim facets, a nacre/iridescent iris) and a darker socket so it reads as an organ.

top_issues.why: The middle polyps, the riptide-plus-headlamp floor, and the wyrm's head at the waterline blow out to pure white, losing form exactly at the focal point.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tone-map or cap emissive stacking so overlaps stay in hue (pale green/cyan) and keep facet shading visible inside the hottest area.

protect: Pressure Polyps: spiky faceted domes in MAELIS sea-green whose light pools on the stone below; a clear hazard silhouette at play size
Real darkness around the creatures in the polyps and riptide frames; the dark is not flattened
Brinewyrm's black hex eye with cyan slit, open toothed jaw and segmented faceted body; strong low-poly silhouette
Riptide's core idea: a glowing eye at the centre of a visible spiral current that lights the floor beneath it
Per-world hue discipline: CRYOS creatures in ice-cyan/white, MAELIS creatures in sea-green
Frostbloom's faceted crystal star as a reveal shape
